problem: Existing open-ended embodied agents (e.g. Voyager, STEVE) chain multiple LLMs/MLMs for perception, planning and action, which is slow and costly. MLMs trained on static data also handle dynamic open-ended scenes poorly, and prior knowledge injected as prompts limits flexibility.
motivation: Open-ended Minecraft tasks such as navigation and creation need multi-granular planning and extra knowledge to resolve vague instructions. Multi-LLM systems give this at high inference cost. Distilling a hierarchical multi-agent teacher, with extra expert knowledge, into a single MLM could keep the performance while removing the runtime prompts and experts.
key_idea: Distill a hierarchical manager/conductor/actor GPT-4V teacher system, augmented with an extra expert (dynamic map or 3D occupancy generator), into a single LLaMA2-13B-based MLM using a DPO loss with DAgger-style sampling.
insight: The ablations show every component matters. Without distillation (w/o KD), goal-search success falls to 12% (8/8/8 LLMs) against 95% for the full model. Without the extra expert (w/o EE), it reaches 45%. The teacher with extra knowledge alone (TO) reaches 51%. The distilled student therefore surpasses its GPT-4V teacher: the expert knowledge shapes the training data and gets baked into the weights, so no expert is needed at inference. Caveat: the paper gives few training details, and the multi-agent gains rely on running several copies of the same model.
method: Hierarchical CPDE system: a manager MLM does centralized planning, conductor MLMs allocate subtasks, and optional actor MLMs execute. The action is a^c = MLM^C(MLM^M(S,T), S_i), and agents are auto-organized (AutoAgents / SOG-inspired).

Multi-modal teacher: GPT-4V (gpt-4-1106-vision-preview) is prompted as Planner, Describer, Critic and Skill modules. It converts observations to text, plans, self-corrects via feedback and simulates plan steps. It uses a multi-modal memory with RAG retrieval of successful plans.

Extra Expert (teacher only): a dynamic map fusing multi-agent observations for navigation, and a modified VQ-VAE producing 3D occupancy (rendered to multi-view images) for building creation. It is P(a|S,t^o)=Σ_g Expert(g|t^o)F_T(a|S,t^o,g), and is not given to the student.
Student architecture: STEVE-13B (ViT encoder + MLP projector + LLaMA2-13B decoder) outputs text actions that are mapped to code actions via a skill library and Mineflayer.

Mirrored hierarchical distillation: the manager, conductor and actor roles are trained in parallel with the teacher on the same inputs. The DPO loss treats teacher actions a* as preferred and student samples as dispreferred. The reference model comes from behavior cloning on a rule-based teacher, and DAgger-style on-policy sampling reduces distribution shift.
Multi-agent deployment: the single distilled MLM runs as multiple agents (up to 8 robots) with a shared dynamic map.

setting.backbone: STEVE-13B (ViT + MLP + LLaMA2-13B), fine-tuned by DPO distillation; teacher GPT-4V (frozen)
setting.training_data: Teacher (GPT-4V) generated action sequences on Minecraft tasks with extra expert knowledge; STEVE-21K dataset for base pretraining; VQ-VAE trained on online 3D building datasets. Scale not stated.
setting.observation: Minecraft egocentric RGB pixels + text task description (image/audio/object goals) + state properties (biome, inventory)
setting.action_space: Textual actions mapped to code skills (Mineflayer APIs)
setting.privileged: Extra expert (dynamic map / 3D occupancy generator) used during training only, not at inference; baselines read info from the game backend.

numbers_note: Custom Minecraft benchmarks with no canonical navigation benchmark. The ablation table reports slightly different multi-agent numbers than the main table (e.g. goal search 95% vs 91%; block search 621 vs 412; map area 1821 vs 1493), and the paper does not explain the discrepancy.
results: STEVE-2 beats Voyager and STEVE in Minecraft navigation and creation. In goal search the 5/8/8-agent version gets 91% success in 4 iterations against 64% for the best baseline (22-29 iterations). Building FID is 21.12 against 68.32 for Creative Agents, and material collection needs 4 iterations against 76 for Voyager. The single distilled 13B model runs at 9.22 s per iteration with 15 GB VRAM, against 28.76 s and 68 GB for STEVE, and it outperforms its GPT-4V teacher.
limitations: Evaluated only in Minecraft on custom tasks and metrics, with no standard embodied navigation benchmark, and the tables are inconsistent (main vs ablation numbers).
Training details are sparse (data scale, DPO hyperparameters), and baselines read information from the game backend while the multi-agent gains still depend on running many copies of the model.
Depends on GPT-4V as the teacher and on hand-built expert modules (a basic VQ-VAE, a dynamic map), so quality is bounded by teacher and expert quality.
